subject: Fix Portfolio.positions concurrency race and unauthenticated docs routes
task:
Fix Portfolio.positions concurrency race and unauthenticated docs routes

Two residuals adjudicated after the scoped re-review of the final-review
fix round -- both fixed directly rather than spun into another agent
round, since they're small and mechanical:

1. The re-review found a new Important: Portfolio.positions returns the
   live self._positions dict (unlike SleeveAccount.positions, fixed in
   this same branch's Task 2), so DashboardReadModel's concurrent
   threadpool reads can hit RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during
   iteration while apply_fill folds a new symbol elsewhere. Fixed with
   the same MappingProxyType(replace(...)) pattern already used for
   SleeveAccount.positions -- and found, while fixing it, that the copy
   itself was still racy: a Python-level dict comprehension iterating
   self._positions.items() directly can be preempted mid-copy by the
   same concurrent mutation. Both properties now take an atomic
   dict(self._positions) snapshot first (a single C-level loop that
   never releases the GIL) before transforming it. Regression tests for
   both add a background writer thread growing the dict while a reader
   iterates positions(); sys.setswitchinterval(1e-6) makes the race
   reliably reproducible rather than intermittent -- confirmed to fail
   on the pre-fix code across three consecutive runs, restored after.

2. The re-review's caveat on M4 (the auth-everywhere test): FastAPI
   mounts /docs, /redoc, and /openapi.json itself, outside every
   router's require_auth dependency, so M4's own OpenAPI-schema
   enumeration structurally cannot see them -- they were reachable
   unauthenticated by default. Disabled all three at app construction
   (docs_url/redoc_url/openapi_url=None) rather than trying to guard
   routes require_auth was never attached to. Corrected require_auth's
   own docstring, which had claimed login/logout were the only
   unauthenticated routes.

Backend: 675 passed, ruff format/check + mypy + docstring lint +
strategy-purity lint + bandit all clean. Frontend: 28/28 passed, clean
vite build.

subject: Fix reconciliation_safe: was 'has a pass ever run', not 'was it safe'
task:
Fix reconciliation_safe: was 'has a pass ever run', not 'was it safe'

Task 11's own review traced this all the way back to Task 1: the heartbeat
computed reconciliation_safe as `loop.last_reconciled_at is not None` --
"has a reconciliation pass ever run", not "was the most recent one safe".
_reconcile_continuously sets last_reconciled_at BEFORE checking the pass's
own result, so a FAILED pass that halts the engine still left that same
iteration's heartbeat reporting reconciliation_safe=True. The Phase 6
dashboard's Resume button reads this exact field to decide whether to

same instant the engine was actually halted on an unresolved break.

_LoopState now tracks last_reconciliation_safe as its own field, set from
report.safe_to_resume directly, never derived from the timestamp. Mutation-
tested: reverted to the original derivation, confirmed the new test fails
with reconciliation_safe=True on a broker holding an unresolved external
order (the exact scenario the bug would misreport), reverted back.

subject: Fix nested mutability gap in SleeveAccount.positions
task:

it does nothing about mutating the object a key points to. PositionView
is a plain mutable dataclass (its own apply_fill mutates qty/avg_cost in
place), so positions["SPY"].qty = x reached through the "read-only" proxy
straight into the sleeve's real bookkeeping, which committed_notional --
and therefore every RiskEngine capital check -- depends on.

reverted to the reference-sharing version, confirmed the new test fails

subject: Reconciler: make the over-fill halt survive later passes and a restart
task:
Reconciler: make the over-fill halt survive later passes and a restart

Review finding F1, a fail-open bug: the two anomalous MISSED_FILL variants
(a broker over-fill, and an unreadable fill price) only blocked resume on the
pass that discovered them. Both checks lived inside _replay_missed_fill, which
was reachable only from "broker_filled > view.filled_qty" -- and that same
method adopted the missing quantity, closing the gap. The next scheduled pass,
and any fresh process rebuilding projections from the log, then reported the
same over-filled order as safe_to_resume=True with no human involvement. That
is exactly the auto-resume CLAUDE.md invariant 7 exists to prevent, and
reconcile_continuous()'s own docstring claimed the opposite.

Split the method in two. _replay_missed_fill now only emits the catch-up
OrderFilled and returns what it adopted; _classify_fill_state runs on every
pass and asks _fill_anomalies whether this order's cumulative state is still
anomalous. Neither anomaly check reads view.filled_qty -- they compare the
broker's own current filled_qty and filled_avg_price against the order's
original submitted_qty, none of which adoption moves -- so the same broker
state keeps producing the same finding forever. _read_fill_price holds the
price parse so it lives in one place.

The kind stays MISSED_FILL on the pass that replays a fill; later passes report
POSITION_BREAK, because nothing is missing by then and what remains is a broker
record this engine cannot explain. Both are unresolved, so the resume decision
is unchanged; only the operator-facing label moves. No new DiscrepancyKind, no
mechanism for clearing a break (deliberately out of scope), and no second
OrderFilled -- verified by replaying the log after four passes.

Also from the same review:

- F2: capture view.filled_qty before _emit folds the replayed fill into that
  same OrderView, so the detail names what was actually missing ("against 4
  locally; replayed the missing 6") instead of the post-replay total.
- F3: correct task-6-report.md 8.1 -- an unfolded Projections produces
  ['external_order', 'position_break'], not NEVER_LANDED. Re-verified by
  running it; it still fails closed either way. (That file is under the
  gitignored .superpowers/ tree, so it is not part of this diff.)
- F4: add the missing regression test pinning NEVER_LANDED for a locally-filled
  order the broker has no record of (surviving mutant MU-H; logic already
  correct, only the test was absent).
- F5: disclose in _replay_missed_fill's docstring that ts_event and ts_init are
  necessarily equal on a replayed fill, matching AlpacaExecutionClient.

565 passed (was 558); mypy, ruff, docstring lint and bandit clean.

subject: Fix C2-R6: clamp the reducing reference to the sleeve's realized position
task:
Fix C2-R6: clamp the reducing reference to the sleeve's realized position

Round 4 asked `is_reducing` about `position_qty + working_qty`. Only the first
half is realized -- `working_qty` is a prediction about orders that can still be
cancelled. A separately-charged fill in the same symbol can carry `position_qty`
through zero without touching a stale working entry, after which the two point
the SAME way and their sum exceeds anything the sleeve holds. An order sized to
that inflated figure was classified "purely position-reducing" while opening
brand-new, entirely unreserved exposure: four orders and zero denials put $5,000
on a $1,000 allocation, a five-order variant breached at a realistic 10%
fat-finger band, and a HALTED sleeve was approved for an order that added
exposure -- the exact outcome round 4's own carve-out ruling said it would never
permit.

New `SleeveAccount.reducing_reference_qty()` clamps the combination into the
closed interval between zero and the realized position, so a still-working
reduction can only ever shrink the allowance toward zero, never grow it or flip
its sign. It is the single accessor `reserve()`, `_check_sleeve_capital` and
`_check_sleeve_halted` all consume -- three hand-written copies of the same
expression drifting apart is the root cause this chain kept re-discovering.

Verified by execution against every repro in the round-4 re-review (all four now
denied or correctly charged), against C2-R4's two-close repro and the round-4
brief's partial-fill scenario (both unchanged), and against round 2/3's five
regression scenarios plus cross-sleeve leakage. Seven independent mutations of
the new code are each caught by a named test, including the re-review's V5
(`_check_sleeve_halted` reading `position_qty` alone), which previously survived
the entire suite.

C2-R5 is untouched by this commit and remains open; see the next one.

subject: Fix M3+M4: reject a non-positive REFUND_SLEEVE amount; deterministic pending() order
task:
Fix M3+M4: reject a non-positive REFUND_SLEEVE amount; deterministic pending() order

M3: Command.__post_init__ only checked that REFUND_SLEEVE's amount was not
None, not that it was positive -- SleeveAccount.refund() applies it
unguarded (allocation += amount), so a negative amount would silently
shrink a sleeve's allocation through a command whose entire purpose is to
grant capacity back. Rejected at construction now.

M4: CommandQueue.pending() ordered only by submitted_at, which is real
wall-clock time (not an injected Clock -- see .submit()'s own docstring),
so two commands submitted in the same instant had no well-defined
processing order. Added command_id as a secondary sort key.

One test each: a negative amount is rejected at construction; two commands
inserted directly with an identical submitted_at (forcing the tie
.submit() itself cannot arrange) come back ordered by command_id, with ids
chosen to sort opposite to insertion order so the assertion actually proves
the tiebreak rather than coincidentally matching insertion order.

subject: Fix I2: memoize MarketCalendar.session_bounds, 5.5ms/call to a dict hit
task:
Fix I2: memoize MarketCalendar.session_bounds, 5.5ms/call to a dict hit

session_bounds() rebuilt a pandas schedule DataFrame via
pandas_market_calendars on every single call -- measured at ~5.4ms and 98%
of RiskEngine.check()'s own total cost, for data that never changes within
a single date. Memoized per date in a plain dict (both the real bounds and
a non-session day's None result), matching CLAUDE.md invariant 3's "sessions
are computed daily, not recomputed on every call."

Verified the caching actually reduces per-call cost, not just that it
compiles: a cold call takes ~210ms in this environment (dominated by
pandas_market_calendars' own schedule computation, not just the theoretical
5.4ms); a second call for the same date is ~0.0002ms, roughly a
million-times speedup. Confirmed via a call-count spy on the underlying
mcal calendar's schedule() method (patch.object(..., wraps=...), so the
real result is still computed and checked correct, not mocked away) that a
repeated call for the same date hits the cache and does not rebuild the
schedule -- for both a real trading day and a non-trading day's None result.

subject: Fix C2: sleeve capital tracks net exposure, not lifetime gross-traded volume
task:
Fix C2: sleeve capital tracks net exposure, not lifetime gross-traded volume

_check_sleeve_capital computed projected = committed_notional + qty*price
regardless of side -- a SELL that closes an existing long added its full
notional to projected exactly like a BUY opening new exposure, so a
fully-committed sleeve could never get flat, violating CLAUDE.md invariant
5's "you can still get flat, you cannot dig deeper" for the exact case it
exists to protect. SleeveAccount.apply_fill() had the same bug: it only ever
accumulated fill_notional, with no path to reduce it when a fill closes
exposure.

Both now evaluate exposure DELTA -- (abs(resulting_qty) - abs(existing_qty))
* price -- instead of gross notional:

- SleeveFill gains symbol/side fields so a fill can be netted against the
  sleeve's own existing position in that symbol; SleeveAccount tracks
  per-symbol net qty and apply_fill's filled_notional now moves by the
  signed exposure delta (negative when reducing, equal to the full fill
  notional when opening fresh from flat -- a strict generalization, not a
  behavior change for any position opened from flat, verified by hand
  against the existing partial-fill tests and confirmed passing unchanged).
- RiskEngine gains a shared _resulting_position_qty helper (used by both
  _check_position_limit, pure refactor, and _check_sleeve_capital) and
  _check_sleeve_capital now projects committed_notional + exposure_delta
  against the allocation. .reserve() intentionally stays gross-notional
  (conservative, documented scope limitation: over-counts a still-working
  reducing order until it fills, the safe direction of error).

New tests: a fully-committed sleeve's SleeveAccount returns to full headroom
after a fully-closing fill; an adding fill counts only its incremental
delta; RiskEngine approves a reducing SELL that closes a fully-committed
position in both ACTIVE and REDUCING state; a SELL with no existing position
(a new short) is still correctly denied.

Also I1: strengthens test_risk_properties.py's
test_no_sequence_of_approved_orders_can_breach_a_sleeve_allocation, which
previously reserved-and-fully-filled every approved order in the same step,
so working_notional was always exactly 0 and the property never generated
the "ten orders each fit individually, collectively breach it" scenario
SleeveAccount exists to guard. Each approved order now draws whether it
fills fully, partially, or stays working unfilled.

Asserts filled_notional + working_notional <= allocation directly, not the
equivalent committed_notional property: mutation-testing (mutating
committed_notional to filled_notional-only, as required) found that
asserting via the composite property does NOT catch that mutation even with
the strengthened sequence, because RiskEngine._check_sleeve_capital reads
that same property to gate approvals, making it self-consistently satisfied
by its own admission decisions regardless of the mutation. Asserting via the
two independently-tracked components breaks that tautology and does fail
against the mutation, confirmed directly.

Updated every SleeveFill(...) construction site across tests/ for the new
required fields (grepped, not discovered via a failing run): test_sleeves.py,
test_risk_properties.py (two sites), and breakers.py's on_fill in production
code. test_sleeves.py's original 9 tests pass unchanged (11/11 with the 2
new ones); test_risk_checks.py's position_limit section confirmed
byte-identical behavior before/after the pure refactor.

subject: Phase 4.1 fix: SleeveAccount.apply_fill handles partial fills correctly
task:
Phase 4.1 fix: SleeveAccount.apply_fill handles partial fills correctly

apply_fill() released a reservation's entire notional the instant any fill
arrived, including a partial one, silently understating committed_notional
for the still-outstanding unfilled portion -- a capital-cap bypass reached
via fill granularity rather than order count. Now a fill reduces the
remaining reservation by its own real notional (qty * price), clamped at
zero, and only fully releases once cumulative fills reach the reserved
amount. No-op for a fill that exactly matches its reservation.

subject: Fix I6: min_backtest_length is vacuous at N=1, weakest on a first evaluation
task:
Fix I6: min_backtest_length is vacuous at N=1, weakest on a first evaluation

min_backtest_length(1, ...) returns 0.0 by design -- one trial has no
selection effect to correct for, and that part is correct and unchanged. But
_min_backtest_length_check used the live n_trials directly as the
threshold's input, so the very first time a (strategy, dataset) pair is ever
evaluated, this check passed on a dataset of any length at all -- exactly
when a strategy is closest to being promoted to Sleeve B.

Floors the trial count used for the threshold at 2 (max(n_trials, 2)),
without changing n_trials itself (still the honest count reported on
GateResult and used by deflated_sharpe). Deliberate, controller-ruled: a
strategy's dataset must clear at least the 2-trial bar even on its
first-ever evaluation.

New test confirms a GateResult computed with n_trials=1 uses
min_backtest_length(2, ...)'s value as its threshold, not 0.0 -- verified it
fails against the pre-fix code (threshold was 0.0, check trivially passed).

subject: Fix I4: multi-symbol backtests crash in Portfolio.mark
task:
Fix I4: multi-symbol backtests crash in Portfolio.mark

run_backtest marked with {bar.symbol: bar.close}, a single-entry dict
containing only the current bar's symbol. On an interleaved multi-symbol bar
stream, the symbol not in the current bar is exactly the previously-filled
position the portfolio is still holding, so Portfolio.mark's fail-loud
"no mark for this open position" guard fired -- a real regression, since
HistoricalDataSource(symbols=[...]) and run_backtest both already treat
multi-symbol streams as first-class.

Now tracks the last-seen close per symbol across the whole bar stream and
marks against that accumulated dict, preserving the fail-loud guarantee for
a symbol the stream has genuinely never sent a bar for.

New test in test_kernel.py interleaves SPY/QQQ bars with a strategy that buys
both and holds; confirmed it reproduces the exact ValueError (on the first
bar marked after both positions are open) before the fix, and that the final
equity curve's positions_value reflects both positions after it.

subject: Fix I2: the -inf sentinel is not valid JSON, Postgres will reject it
task:
Fix I2: the -inf sentinel is not valid JSON, Postgres will reject it

_INSUFFICIENT_DATA_SHARPE (float("-inf")) was written straight into
research_trials.metrics, a JSON column. -Infinity is not a legal JSON number
under RFC 8259; SQLite's permissive JSON1 extension (every test here runs
against sqlite:///:memory:) accepts it, Postgres's stricter JSON/JSONB parser
does not.

TrialLog.record now sanitizes non-finite metric values to JSON null before
the insert (_json_safe_metrics), and _row_to_trial_record reverses null back
to -inf on read (_floats_from_json_safe) -- the only non-finite value this
codebase ever produces, so the reversal is unambiguous. TrialRecord.metrics's
Python-side type and every existing comparison stay exactly -inf/float; only
the on-disk representation changes.

No Postgres is provisioned in this environment, so this is verified at the
string level: a new test confirms the raw stored row (queried directly,
bypassing TrialLog's own read-path reversal) has None where -inf was logged,
and that re-serializing it contains neither "Infinity" nor "NaN" -- the
literal tokens Postgres's parser would reject. A live-Postgres round-trip
test is deferred until Postgres is provisioned (Phase 4/5 or CI), consistent
with every other persistence module in this codebase being SQLite-only-tested
today, not a new gap.

subject: Fix C1: evaluate_gate crashes on a never-trading config
task:
Fix C1: evaluate_gate crashes on a never-trading config

sharpe_ratio raises ValueError on zero-variance returns (a flat equity curve, e.g.
a config whose slow SMA never forms so it never trades). Two call sites only
guarded the <2-observation case: run_trial (trials.py) and
_deflated_sharpe_check's direct full-dataset backtest (gate.py), which crashed
evaluate_gate outright instead of returning a GateResult whose min_trades check
exists to catch exactly this configuration.

Both now catch the zero-variance ValueError and report it as a failing check
(gate.py) or the existing -inf sentinel (trials.py), never letting the
exception propagate out of evaluate_gate.

subject: Phase 3.3: prevent _aggregate_sharpe from splicing bars across a rolling-mode purge gap
task:
Phase 3.3: prevent _aggregate_sharpe from splicing bars across a rolling-mode purge gap

_aggregate_sharpe previously ran one backtest over the flattened union of every
fold's train (or test) indices. That's correct only when the union is a single
contiguous block (true for anchored mode, and rolling mode with label_horizon=0).
Rolling mode with label_horizon>0 purges label_horizon bars off the right edge of
each fold's own train window, opening a real gap between consecutive folds' train
windows -- flattening across that gap spliced bar N to bar N+label_horizon+1 as if
temporally adjacent, silently blending pre-/post-gap prices in any strategy that
carries state across bars (e.g. MovingAverageCrossover's rolling close window).

Fix: split the index union into maximal contiguous runs (_contiguous_runs), run one
independent fresh-strategy backtest per run, and pool the resulting *returns* (never
raw bars) before scoring one Sharpe. Degenerates to the previous single-backtest
behavior when the union is already one contiguous block, so both control tests'
numbers are bit-for-bit unchanged (confirmed by direct re-run). New regression test
uses anchored=False with label_horizon=100 to exercise the multi-block path, and
checks run_walk_forward's is_sharpe against two independent reference computations
(one per-block/pooled, one spliced) that provably disagree with each other.

subject: fix: escape search terms in PostgREST or() filters
task:
fix: escape search terms in PostgREST or() filters

The directory search box was interpolated straight into an or() expression,
which PostgREST parses by splitting on commas and parentheses. Searching for a
name or a city containing a comma returned PGRST100 and a 400 -- the workhorse
screen of the app, broken by ordinary input. A crafted term could also append
filter clauses of its own; RLS still held, but the results were not what the
query intended.

Wrapping the value in double quotes is PostgREST's documented way to make those
characters literal. Verified against the live API before and after.

Wildcards are stripped rather than escaped: ilike has no ESCAPE clause over the
REST interface, so a literal percent sign cannot be expressed, and silently
widening someone's search is worse than ignoring a character they almost
certainly did not mean as a wildcard.

searchCommunities already had an ad-hoc version of this fix, stripping the same
characters and losing the match in the process. Both call sites now share one
helper.

subject: Fix C2-R5: an exemption's cover cannot be spent by a different order
task:
Fix C2-R5: an exemption's cover cannot be spent by a different order

A reducing order is exempted from capital reservation because filling it can
only shrink exposure. That is true only while the position it was judged against
is still there. A DIFFERENT order for the same symbol -- correctly judged
non-reducing, correctly charged its own honest notional -- could fill first and
take those shares, after which the stranded exemption opened brand-new exposure
with nothing reserved: $1,000.22 committed on a $1,000 cap in three orders.

Two rules, both scoped to the direction that can actually do the damage:

  Rule A (`SleeveAccount.consumes_a_working_reduction`, denied in check 10):
  refuse any order pointing the same way as an outstanding exemption that is not
  itself small enough to be exempted out of what that exemption left over.
  Charging such an order prices its own exposure honestly and says nothing about
  the exemption it strands.

  Rule B (`charged_qty_toward_zero`, folded into `reducing_reference_qty`):
  grant no exemption at all while a charged order is already working toward the
  same zero. This closes the mirror-image ordering -- the thief submitted FIRST,
  where there is no exemption yet for Rule A to protect -- which is exactly the
  counterexample that disproved Rule A on its own in round 4.

Together they keep an exemption and a same-direction charge from ever coexisting
in one symbol, so total quantity working toward zero never exceeds the realized
position, so every outstanding exemption is still genuinely reducing when it
fills. Charged orders need their own signed-quantity ledger for this;
`working_notional` is deliberately left as `sum(self._reservations.values())`,
byte-identical.

The behavioural price, stated plainly: while a reducing order rests, a second
same-side order for that symbol is refused unless it fits the shares the first
left over. Two closes summing to no more than the position are still both
exempted; a second FULL close while the first rests is not -- cancel it first,
or size the new one to fit. Adding to a position while a protective close rests
is untouched.

Verified by execution: both C2-R5 orderings from the round-4 report now denied;
the round-4 brief's partial-fill case, the two-concurrent-exemptions case, the
re-quote path, cross-symbol independence and cancel-then-resize all still behave;
4,000 randomized orders show 0 check()/reserve() disagreements; a fuzzer that
flushes every still-working order in EVERY permutation finds no breach. The
`strict=True` C2-R5 xfail tripwire is now a passing regression test, and the
deferred-fill property's xfail came off with it.

Known residual, measured not assumed, and unchanged from rounds 3 and 4 (checked
against 68fec7f and e452eb3): a broker OVER-fill can still strand a sibling
exemption, because it moves the position by more than the working quantity it
consumes. Documented in `_check_sleeve_capital`.

Part 4: the one-sleeve route round 4 opened to an unpriced BUY-to-cover reaching
`buying_power` ungated is closed by round 5's clamp -- an exemption now requires
a realized sleeve position, and with one sleeve that implies a realized global
one. The two docstrings' "two sleeves" wording is accurate again; both now say
so and say why.

subject: Fix C2 round 4: working orders count against is_reducing; halted sleeve can get flat
task:
Fix C2 round 4: working orders count against is_reducing; halted sleeve can get flat

Two Criticals from the round-3 independent re-review.

C2-R4: reserve() and _check_sleeve_capital both asked is_reducing against the
FILLED position alone, so N ordinary closing orders queued before any of them
filled were each independently judged "can only shrink the position" against the
same stale number, each reserved nothing, and collectively flipped the position
and breached the sleeve cap by an unbounded multiple with zero denials. Two
orders suffice -- a resting broker-side stop plus a strategy exit, CLAUDE.md
invariant 8's own prescribed shape. SleeveAccount now tracks a per-order,
per-symbol signed working quantity for every order reserve() judged reducing,
and both ledgers ask is_reducing against filled-plus-working. Verified: the
two-close repro now denies the second order (committed 2000 on a 1000 cap
before, 0 breach after); N=2,3,5,11,21 all deny at the second attempt; a
partially-filled close's own remainder stays correctly exempt; and 20,000
randomized single orders still show 0 check()/reserve() disagreements.

Only reducing orders contribute to the new ledger. Folding a non-reducing
order's hypothetical fill into the reducing test would recreate the identical
bug one level up: a later order exempted against a position that evaporates if
the BUY it was counting on is cancelled instead of filling.

C2-remainder (the original C2's untouched second half): check 2 denied EVERY
intent for a halted sleeve, a pure close included -- reachable by design, since
check 10 approves at exactly projected == allocation, is_exhausted is
headroom <= 0, and _evaluate_sleeve_exhaustion then halts the sleeve. CLAUDE.md
invariant 5's "you can still get flat, you cannot dig deeper" was false at
Sleeve A's own designed steady state. A halted sleeve now gets the same carve-out
the engine-wide REDUCING state gives everything else, judged against the sleeve's
own filled-plus-working exposure rather than the global Portfolio.

apply_fill's working-quantity decrement clamps at zero rather than letting an
over-fill flip the remainder's sign, mirroring the max(Decimal(0), ...) clamp the
notional decrement already applies -- verified that the unclamped form fabricates
phantom exposure that exempts a later order from any reservation.

Also corrects four now-false docstrings: the module-level price-safety posture and
_check_buying_power's unreachability claim (both falsified by round 3's no-price
change), _resulting_position_qty's "shared with _check_sleeve_capital", and the
Portfolio-partitioning paragraph's omission of check 1 as a global reader.

_check_position_limit is byte-identical to 68fec7f (sha256 of the extracted method
body), as are _check_trading_state, _check_gross_exposure and
_check_order_rate_limit. Eight independent mutations of the new code are each
caught by a named test.
